findings.claim:
In all four packages, the step 'put them into the two lever splices' still cannot be done in place, for three reasons.
(1) The levers' grip ends are blocked by the channel's top flange. The splices stand from z 28.5 to 46.8, entries down, and the flange's underside is at z 46.8, a 0 gap. Per WAGO's drawing (221-412_K007), each lever hinges at the entry end and lifts at the far end, which is the top end here. No thumb, nail or blade can reach that end. The sides are no better: the gaps are 0.35, 0.5 and 0.75.
(2) The real part does not fit. WAGO's own data sheet gives 13.2 x 8.6 x 18.8 (18.6 by its inch figure). The pocket between the ledge's top (z 28.3) and the flange is 18.5. The CAD draws 18.3 x 13.1 x 8.2.
(3) The splices cannot be wired in hand and pushed back either. The LED leads are cut to exactly the drawn route plus the 11 inside (135.7 and 148.6, against 136 and 149), so they have no slack.
The swing room in front of the levers is real (the lane's box is clear), but nothing tests the access to their grip ends.
The fix is small and stays inside the channel:
- give a real splice 4 to 5 above it: lower the ledge (formed as the callout describes, its top lands at z 26.7, a 20.1 pocket, still only 1.3 to 1.5 above a real splice), or cut the flange back over the splices' tops;
- or ship the splices with their levers open and say so;
- add 20 to 30 of slack to each LED lead, held by a tie.

The splices' ledge, as drawn, cannot be made the way the callout says ('the window's top edge bent out +y').
- The window's tab is 25 x 5.7.
- Bent at its top edge, it lies at z 25.1 to 26.7: its top face is at 26.7, not 28.3.
- It reaches about 4 past the R 1.6 bend, not 7.4.
- It is 25 wide and cannot join the side flanges. The drawing shows 27.8 wide, merged into both.
The drawing should show the ledge as formed (this also sets the pocket's height; see the blocking finding), or make it a separate part.

The straps' stop is real: moved 1.0, they touch the web with 0 overlap; moved 1.05, they overlap. But the tightened seat is a D, 6.0 wide and 5.0 deep (26.1 mm2), because the strap's tip and leg also bound the cord at x ±3.
- A 6.0 cord loses 7.6 % of its section, a 6.25 cord 15 %, and a 6.5 cord 21 % (1.5 in y and 0.5 in x). The rows say '1.0 to 1.5'.
- Whether 21 % damages the jacket (UL 1598 5.15.1.2) is for the prototype. It is cheaper to narrow the range to about 6.0 to 6.3, or to open the legs to about 6.6.
The slip at 156 N is UNVERIFIED. The thin end (6.0, squeezed 1.0) is the weak case for 17.21.1, so test both ends of the range.
The straps' sheet does not let a shop make them:
- it gives only 16 x 13 x 6 overall;
- it omits the ring's Ø6.0 ID, the 1.0 offset of the foot and tip that sets the stop, the Ø3.4 hole and the spring steel's temper;
- the BOM counts 1 per lamp, though there are two straps.
The cord's '6.0 to 6.5 over the braid' still has no maker and no sheet ('any (UL listed)').

NOT READY in this lens, and the verdict is the same for all four packages. A without the lock (the pick), A with the lock (the same canopy turned 105 deg), today and B measure identically, with 0 clashes at zero tolerance.
The re-laid-out corner is a real step: the strap screws are reachable, the driver sits on ERP's holes, and the tray's joint can be made in principle. But the splices still cannot be worked in place: their levers' grip ends touch the channel's flange, WAGO's real 221-412 (18.6 to 18.8 deep) is taller than the 18.5 pocket, and the LED leads have no slack.
One geometry pass inside 150 x 50 fixes that. With the small fixes alongside (the flange's 245 MPa at 156 N, the web nut's 4.0 edge distance, the ledge's forming, the 120 deg roll, the fold fit, ties and slack, the cord step's order, the stale notes), it is ready after small fixes. Nothing here needs the owner.

verdicts.reason:
The core of this finding does not hold, because the reviewer modeled the lever backwards. On the 221-412 the lever pivots at the end away from the entries, and you lift it by its nose, which sits over the entries.

Evidence:
- AutomationDirect's 221-412_K007 is a vector PDF (https://cdn.automationdirect.com/static/drawings/2d/221-412_K007-0000.pdf). I fitted its 40-point phantom polyline (py/pdfpoly.py, out/side_polys.json). The open lever's back line stands 3.63 from the far end and rises to 15.34 overall. The arc (R 18.61, centered on that line) runs down to the top corner at the entry end, so it is the nose's path.
- WAGO's own data sheet (221-412, version 03.10.2022, p.1 photos; https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/780/DOC031780068.pdf) shows the open lever standing on the back half of the housing, with the clamp exposed at the entry end.

With entries down, the grips are the noses at the bottom, not at the flange. The reviewer's 0-gap slab and the 0.21 mm3 rub come from a lever drawn to the housing's far end and hinged at the wrong end (canopy-wired/py/probe_splice.py). With K007's real outline, the levers open clear in all four packages: 1.0 to the stud nuts in front of both cord levers and 0.77 to 0.87 to the channel (out/k007-*.json).

What survives is should-fix, not blocking:
- (2) WAGO's own sheet and drawing give a depth of 18.8 (13.2 wide, 8.4 to 8.6 high), against the 18.5 pocket (crystal.py:990, :995, :1015). That pocket cannot be made as drawn anyway; see the ledge finding.
- (3) The LED leads are exactly the route plus 11 (my out/handcalc.txt: 135.7 and 148.6, against 136 and 149).

The real access limit is the ledge under the noses (see missed).

Confirmed on my own build of a56c5b8bd6 (out/corner-Aoff.txt, py/corner.py).
- The side flanges' inner faces are at x -3.4 and 24.4 (27.8 apart). The splices run x -3.05 to 10.05 and 10.55 to 23.65.
- With the called 0.5 dimples (crystal.py:1013, :1269), the clearance is 0.1 with the drawn gap and 0.6 with the splices pushed together. That is a clearance, not a push fit.
- No maker's figure turns it into interference. WAGO's own data sheet (Mar 2018) gives 13.1 wide; AutomationDirect's drawing gives 13.0.
- The ledge is drawn x -3.4 to 24.4, y 4.6 to 12.0, z 26.7 to 28.3 (crystal.py:995) and is merged into both side flanges. The callout (crystal.py:1269) says it is the 25 x 5.7 window's tab (crystal.py:994), bent out about its top edge. Bent that way, the tab would sit at z 25.1 to 26.7 and reach only about y 10.3, less the bend, and it could not join the flanges. So the reviewer's point about the ledge holds.

Two things are overstated:
- As drawn, the notches are closed slots (my ray at y 11.8 is solid from x -5 to 26). In the CAD, the wires do hold the splices in +y to within about 1.8. They are lost only once the ledge is made as the real tab.
- 'UL 1598 6.17.2 relies on this fixed place' overstates the code stakes. The 4th edition has no US clause requiring a splice to be fixed; 6.18.2's 'mechanically secure' is the Mexican deviation. 6.17.2.2's 6.4 mm separation is kept even by a loose splice 21 to 28 from the slots.

It is still a should-fix: the sheets claim a hold the geometry does not give, and the ledge cannot be made as drawn.

On the fix:
- Prefer the tie through two slots in the web. On a bent-tab ledge, the fingers left between the four 4-wide notches are only 1.25 to 3.1 wide. That is no room for the LED leads' tie slots that V11.md plans 'in the ledge'.
- The coordinator's notes name a later commit, f7ede2f179 (tie slots and dimples). It is not in the local repo, and I did not check it.

The weights reproduce (out/weights.txt, by the lane's own method from my solids):
- the plate and all on it 717 g; the lamps 1590 to 1712 g; the canopy 317 g;
- 2.62 to 2.75 kg in all, and 1.65 to 1.73 kg with the shade off.
NOTES also give no next step after 'hold the plate' (crystal.py:1733-1735).

But 'that is a two-person job' does not hold:
- UL 1598 4th ed. 11.5.1 lets 'a luminaire weighing 4.54 kg (10 lb) or less, excluding diffusers, light-directing parts, and decorative parts, ... be removed to provide access to branch circuit connections'. Here that weight is about 1.7 kg.
- 11.5.2 asks for separate support only above 4.5 kg on the wiring.
- NOTES' own OPEN (3) already relies on 11.5.1.
- One person can hold 1.7 to 2.7 kg in one hand while opening two connectors. One can also hang the plate on one box screw through its closed slot, as in (2).

So this is a nit-level text improvement (shade off first; hang it on one box screw), not a should-fix. The bigger gap in this paragraph is the loose canopy (see missed).

THE CORD'S STRAPS ARE '1.0 ZINC-PLATED SPRING STEEL' WITH NO GRADE, HARDNESS OR BAKE (crystal.py:1144; the straps have no callout) (minor).

- These straps are the cord's only strain relief in the canopy.
- Each strap stops on the web, so spring temper gains nothing. Call plain low-carbon steel or 301/304 stainless, or give the hardness and the bake.
